Precipitation in the HUC8 watersheds is calculated using a gridded daily (24‐hr period ending at 1200 UTC) product from the PRISM
interpolated to a 4 km × 4 km grid using digital elevation model and other topographic data sets

chunks.text: Synoptic and moisture variables are taken from the ERA5 reanalysis at 0.25° × 0.25° resolution, using 0000 UTC fields. The k-means clustering is initialized with least-correlated ERA5 variables such as 700-hPa specific humidity and winds/temperature at 700 and 500 hPa averaged across Colorado. ERA5 also supports the composite and case-study analyses.
supporting_quote: The ERA5 global gridded reanalysis variables with 0.25° × 0.25° grid spacing were obtained at 0000 UTC
least correlated meteorological variables from the ERA5 reanalysis, such as 700‐hPa specific humidity, winds and temperature at 700‐hPa and 500‐hPa averaged across the state boundaries of CO.

chunks.text: Atmospheric river occurrence is taken from the Guan & Waliser (2024) global AR database based on ERA5. The AR detection thresholds include seasonal IVT percentile criteria and a minimum IVT of 100 kg m−1 s−1, plus feature geometry constraints (length and length-to-width ratio). The study uses this catalog to compute AR fractions and anomalous AR probabilities within regimes.
supporting_quote: We used a catalog of ARs developed by Guan & Waliser (2024) using the ERA5 data set
The IVT threshold for AR detection was specified seasonally, ranging from the 85th to 95th percentile, with a lower limit of 100 kg m−1 s−1.

chunks.text: K-means clustering of 3,025 top-decile precipitation days yields four regimes with distinct seasonal occurrence. Regime 1 occurs in winter and represents 19% of top-decile days. Regime 2 is cool-season with spring/fall emphasis and represents 24%, regime 3 represents the lowest fraction at 15%, and warm-season regime 4 accounts for the largest share at 42%.
supporting_quote: We applied k‐means clustering to categorize regimes over the 3,025 top‐decile precipitation days in CO.
Regime 1 occurs during the winter months and accounts for 19% of top‐ decile precipitation days.
Regime 2 ... containing 24% of top‐decile precipitation days.
Regime 3 accountsfor the lowest fraction (15%) of top‐decile precipitation days.
Regime 4 occurs during the warm season and accounts for the largest fraction (42%) of top‐decile precipitation days.

chunks.text: The regimes differ in where AR frequency maxima occur, indicating distinct moisture pathways. Regime 1 shows high AR frequency along the West Coast and over the Southwest U.S. Regimes 2 and 3 show maxima over the Central/Southern Plains with inland extension from the Gulf of America, with regime 3 concentrated over the Southern Plains and Lower Mississippi River Valley. Regime 4 shows frequent AR-like features over the Central Plains farther west near the Rockies with an inland extension from the western Gulf of America along the Rio Grande Valley.
supporting_quote: Regime 1 ARs along the West Coast and over the Southwest U.S.
Regime 2 features a prominent maximum in AR frequency over the Central and Southern Plains
Regime 3 ... a maximum in AR frequency over the Southern Plains and the Lower Mississippi River Valley, with an extension inland from the Gulf of America.

Regime 4 features a high frequency of ARs over the Central Plains located farther west along the foothills of the Rockies, with an inland extension from the western Gulf of America along the Rio Grande Valley.

chunks.text: Composite synoptic patterns indicate regime 1 is linked to a trough in the subtropical jet and a lee cyclone, with moisture transport into western Colorado via northwesterly and southwesterly IVT from landfalling West Coast ARs. Much of the landfall IVT is blocked by coastal ranges, but some penetrates inland through gaps and produces extreme precipitation on western slopes. The regime’s heavy precipitation focuses on the northern mountains, San Juan, and Elk Mountains.
supporting_quote: The composite of 500‐hPa geopotential heights and SLP in regime 1 feature a trough in the subtropical jet and a surface lee cyclone
transport inland to CO via northwesterly and southwesterly IVT
some of the moisture penetrates through the topographic gaps and impacts the western slopes in CO.
The northern mountains, the San Juan mountains, and the Elk mountains in western CO receive a significant amount of extreme precipitation in this regime

chunks.text: Regime 2 features an amplified trough over the Intermountain West and lower sea-level pressure over Colorado, enabling both southwesterly and southeasterly IVT into the state. This reflects combined influence of ARs landfalling along the West Coast of Mexico and the Gulf of America. Extreme precipitation is concentrated over the San Juan and Elk Mountains in southwest Colorado, and a highlighted example is the March 2019 event that produced 132 cm of snow at Wolf Creek Pass.
supporting_quote: Regime 2 featured an amplified trough over the Intermountain West and lower sea‐level pressure over CO
This deeper trough facilitated both southwesterly and southeasterly transport of IVT into CO associated with ARs landfalling along the West Coast (of Mexico) and the Gulf of America
Extreme precipitation during regime 2 is mostly observed over the San Juan and Elk mountains in southwest CO
March 2019, which produced 132 cm (52 inches) of snow at Wolf Creek Pass

chunks.text: Regime 3 is characterized by an amplified trough and a cut-off low over the Great Plains, with high IVT extending north from the Gulf of America into the Front Range and eastern Colorado. The paper notes that regime 3 can follow regime 2 as the Intermountain West trough moves eastward, with lee cyclogenesis aiding poleward moisture transport. Example storms include the 17–19 March 2003 event that produced more than 7 feet of snow in Denver.
supporting_quote: Regime 3 also featured an amplified trough at 500 hPa with a cut‐off low at 700 hPa over the Great Plains and high IVT extending north from the Gulf of America into the Front Range and eastern CO
This regime typically occurs in immediate succession to regime 2 as the trough from the Intermountain West moves eastward into the Great Plains.
The March 2003 storm, which resulted in more than 7 feet of snow in Denver

chunks.text: Regime 4 is a warm-season pattern with ridging over Colorado associated with a northward/westward-shifted NASH and development of the summer continental anticyclone. It coincides with NAM onset and moisture transport into the Southwest U.S. from both the Gulf of California and the Gulf of America. The regime has potential for flash flooding from persistent rain affecting the Front Range and southern Colorado, including the September 2013 floods.
supporting_quote: Regime 4 contains ridging over CO coincident with a northward and westward shift of the NASH
This pattern coincides with the onset of the NAM in July with poleward transport of water vapor into the Southwest U.S. from both the Gulf of California and the Gulf of America
This regime has a large potential for flash flooding through persistent rain impacting the Front Range and southern CO
The flash floods in September 2013 ... occurred within this regime.

chunks.text: In regime 1, anomalous AR probability is elevated along the West Coast from two days before through the event day. The analysis indicates a southward-elongating trough that increases contributions along California and Baja by day −1, and continues into day 0. Regime 1 precipitation is largely AR-associated, with about 87% of top-decile precipitation in this regime tied to a West Coast AR.
supporting_quote: Regime 1 contains a high frequency of anomalous ARs landfalling on the West Coast from day − 2 to day 0
nearly 87% of top‐decile precipitation in regime 1 is associated with an AR located along the West Coast

chunks.text: Regime 2 shows anomalous AR probability near Southern California and Baja supported by a shortwave trough over the Intermountain West that extends southward toward the event day. Both West Coast and Gulf of America ARs can influence Colorado in this regime. The computed precipitation contributions indicate 70% from West Coast ARs and 25% from Gulf of America ARs, with some years reaching 100% coincidence between annual top-decile precipitation and ARs.
supporting_quote: Regime 2 contains an anomalous AR probability along the coast of Southern California and the Baja Peninsula supported by a shortwave trough in the Intermountain West.
Overall, 70% of the top‐decile precipitation is from the West Coast ARs and 25% from the Gulf of America ARs.
regime 2 is clearly influenced by ARs, with a 100% of the annual top‐decile precipitation coincident with ARs in several years

chunks.text: Regime 3 exhibits a transition from decreasing West Coast AR probabilities to increasing Gulf of America AR probabilities as a shortwave trough propagates eastward into the Great Plains. On the event day, AR anomalies are exclusively from Gulf of America ARs. These Gulf ARs contribute 76% of regime 3 top-decile precipitation, while the remaining non-AR precipitation is attributed to upslope flow and barrier-jet effects along the Front Range.
supporting_quote: illustrates the eastward propagation of a shortwave trough from the Intermountain West to the Great Plains region
Day 0 has exclusively Gulf of America ARs, which contribute to 76% of the top‐decile precipitation in regime 3
The non‐AR precipitation is likely due to topography induced upslope flow and barrier jets along the Front Range

chunks.text: Warm-season regime 4 shows relatively stationary 700-hPa heights from day −2 to day 0 and does not exhibit a strong signal of anomalous AR probability. The paper argues that warm-season AR-like IVT does not require an extratropical cyclone to penetrate inland; instead, seasonal circulation (northward-shifted NASH and NAM onset) enables moisture transport. About 60% of top-decile precipitation in regime 4 is contributed by strong IVT resembling ARs linked to combinations of lee cyclones/LLJs, NASH anticyclonic flow, and the thermally driven GPLLJ.
supporting_quote: regime 4 contains relatively stationary geopotential heights at 700 hPa from day − 2 to day 0
This regime does not have a significant contribution from anomalous ARs.

Nearly 60% of top‐ decile precipitation is contributed by strong IVT resembling ARs due to combinations of lee cyclones (and their LLJ), anticyclonic flow around the NASH, and the thermally driven GPLLJ in regime 4

chunks.text: A methodological limitation is that ARs are identified solely as IVT features, rather than being classified by the underlying dynamical mechanisms that produce the transport. Processes such as baroclinic low-level jets, anticyclonic flow around NASH, and other drivers are not part of AR detection itself. Instead, those mechanisms are inferred indirectly via the regime categorization and synoptic interpretation.
supporting_quote: It should be noted here that ARs were identified based solely on IVT features.

The underlying physical processes responsible for the transport of water vapor in West Coast and Gulf of America ARs such as baroclinic LLJ, NASH circulation, etc., are instead represented through the categorization of precipitation regimes.

chunks.text: The authors caution that positive AR probability and IVT anomalies over the Gulf of America during cool-season regimes represent anomalies in both timing and season compared to the thermally driven nocturnal GPLLJ typical of the warm season. This highlights that similar IVT signatures can occur under different seasonal dynamics, complicating direct comparison of AR-like transport between cool- and warm-season regimes. Interpreting AR signals therefore requires attention to seasonally varying background circulation.
supporting_quote: the positive anomalies in AR probability ... over the Gulf of America in cool season regimes 1, 2, and 3 are anomalous in both timing and season relative to the thermally driven nocturnal GPLLJ that dominates the warm season regime.

chunks.text: The study positions the regime classification as a basis for predictability assessment rather than a complete forecast verification analysis. It states that subsequent work will examine forecast skill of extreme precipitation events and model forecast errors across lead times. This implies that the present paper does not directly quantify forecast performance, but instead builds a storm-typing framework to enable that evaluation.
supporting_quote: The categorization of extreme precipitation into AR‐related versus non‐AR related in synoptic regimes is useful ... to assess regime‐dependent predictability
Subsequent analyses will focus on the forecast skill of extreme precipitation events and evaluating model forecast errors across multiple lead timesto improve process‐based understanding

chunks.text: The paper concludes that four distinct synoptic regimes explain top-decile precipitation variability in Colorado from 1981–2023, separating cool-season and warm-season patterns and their moisture pathways. Cool-season regimes feature anomalous ARs supported by troughs that enable inland penetration from the West Coast and/or strong Gulf of America transport into eastern Colorado. Warm-season extremes are linked more to seasonal circulation (NASH/NAM) and strong IVT, with less dependence on anomalous AR probabilities.
supporting_quote: Four distinct synoptic patterns or regimes contributing to top‐decile precipitation in Colorado were investigated from 1981 to 2023.
During the cool season ... characterized by an anomalously high frequency of landfalling ARs along the Pacific Northwest, California, and Baja Peninsula coasts
In contrast, most warm season precipitation was not associated with anomalous ARs but instead with water vapor transport related to the North Atlantic subtropical high and Monsoon high

chunks.text: A key takeaway is that ARs are major contributors to Colorado precipitation extremes, with both West Coast and Gulf of America sources playing important roles. The study reports that West Coast and Gulf of America ARs contribute 32% and 43% of top-decile precipitation statewide, respectively. This supports using an AR-informed storm-typing approach to improve understanding and evaluation of extreme precipitation drivers in Colorado.
supporting_quote: West Coast and Gulf of America ARs contributed to 32% and 43% of top‐decile precipitation in CO, respectively.
The categorization of extreme precipitation into AR‐related versus non‐AR related in synoptic regimes is useful for the purposes of storm‐typing

chunks.text: Extreme precipitation events (EPEs) in the Southeastern United States (SEUS) arise from multiple storm processes and moisture pathways, including cool-season frontal systems and atmospheric rivers (ARs) and warm-season thunderstorms and tropical cyclones (TCs). Moisture feeding these events commonly originates from the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean Sea, and Atlantic Ocean. Observed changes show increasing warm-season extremes and decreasing cool-season extremes, with intensifying multi-day and sub-daily extremes. This diversity of mechanisms motivates separating events by storm type and circulation pattern to understand impacts and predictability.
supporting_quote: These extreme precipitation events (EPEs) in the SEUS are primarily caused by cool‐season frontal systems and atmospheric rivers (ARs)
warm‐season thunderstorms and landfalling tropical cyclones (TCs; ... ) with moisture sources from the Gulf of Mexico, the Caribbean Sea, and the Atlantic Ocean
Long‐term trends ... illustrate an increasing trend in warm‐season EPEs and a decreasing trend in cool‐season EPEs

chunks.text: Prior literature indicates substantial seasonal contributions of different storm types to SEUS EPEs: ARs are prominent in the cool season, while TCs and MCSs contribute strongly in the warm season. These processes can also occur concurrently (e.g., mixtures of ARs with TCs or MCSs). Non-TC EPEs linked to ARs and MCSs are more frequent in inland/western portions of the SEUS, whereas TC-influenced extremes are more coastal. This motivates explicitly quantifying joint occurrences rather than treating storm types as mutually exclusive.
supporting_quote: more than 50% of warm‐season EPEs in the SEUS are associated with TCs ... while approximately 15% are associated with MCSs
Similarly, 40% of cool‐season EPEs in the SEUS are associated with ARs
These processes are not mutually exclusive.

chunks.text: Extreme quantitative precipitation forecast (QPF) skill in the SEUS is generally lower than in other U.S. regions, partly because warm-season convective extremes are poorly detected. Skill is known to depend on event type: long-duration synoptic-scale events and events with strong integrated vapor transport (IVT) tend to have higher skill than short-duration convective events. Skill also declines with increasing lead time. However, how large-scale circulation patterns and storm-type mixtures condition extreme QPF skill in the SEUS has been less explored.
supporting_quote: The SEUS typically has lower extreme quantitative precipitation forecast (QPF) skill than regions in the northeastern, western, and central US due to poor detection of warm‐season convective EPEs
EPEs associated with strong integrated vapor transport (IVT) contain higher QPF skill than those with weak IVT, and the extreme QPF skill decreases with increasing lead time in the SEUS
not much is known about the extreme QPF skill of large‐scale circulation patterns associated with various storm types such as ARs, MCSs, and TCs in the SEUS

chunks.text: The study tests the hypothesis that SEUS extreme QPF skill depends on storm type (ARs, MCSs, TCs) and their embedding synoptic patterns. It aims to identify distinct synoptic patterns linked to EPEs across seasons, quantify the contribution of ARs/MCSs/TCs (including coincident occurrences) within each pattern, and evaluate extreme QPF skill for these patterns at 1–3 day lead times. The intent is to explain why some EPEs are more predictable than others in the SEUS using a pattern- and storm-type perspective.
supporting_quote: We hypothesize that this extreme QPF skill is influenced by different storm types, such as atmospheric rivers (ARs), mesoscale convective systems (MCSs), and tropical cyclones (TCs), occurring within various synoptic patterns.

the objectives of the current analysis are to (a) identify distinct synoptic patterns ...; (b) investigate the contribution of storm types ...; and (c) evaluate the extreme QPF skill ... at lead times of 1, 2, and 3 days.

chunks.text: Operationally relevant forecast skill for extreme precipitation in the SEUS is comparatively low, especially for warm-season convective events. This creates challenges for anticipating high-impact floods and related hazards. Prior work suggests high-IVT events are more predictable, but the SEUS features mixed storm processes where ARs, MCSs, and TCs can coincide. The lack of detailed understanding of how synoptic patterns and storm-type mixtures control predictability is the central gap addressed.
supporting_quote: The Southeastern United States (SEUS) region has lower extreme quantitative precipitation forecast(QPF)skill compared to the northeastern or western United States.
The variety of storm processes that trigger EPEs makes it difficult to predict their characteristics and impacts
not much is known about the extreme QPF skill of large‐scale circulation patterns associated with various storm types such as ARs, MCSs, and TCs in the SEUS.

chunks.text: Extreme precipitation days were defined using domain-averaged PRISM QPE within a specified box and then clustered into synoptic patterns using KMeans. Ten ERA5 variables sampled at three stations (KJAN, KBNA, KATL) were used as clustering inputs, including surface pressure, surface-based CAPE, humidity at 700/850 hPa, and winds/temperature at 850/700/500 hPa. The number of clusters was selected by testing k=2–10 and choosing six using minimal similarity plus validity indices (sum of squared distances and Davies–Bouldin score). Pattern interpretation used composites of meteorological fields over associated days.
supporting_quote: EPEs are identified ... using a 90th percentile DAP threshold of 10 mm across wet days.
we employed the KMeans clustering algorithm, which can flexibly process 10 variables as input
The algorithm was initialized with k values ranging from 2 to 10, and the optimal value of six was selected
validated using cluster validity indices, including the sum ofsquared distances ... and the Davies‐ Bouldin score

chunks.text: Storm-type contributions were computed using dedicated detection datasets/algorithms for ARs, MCSs, and TCs. ARs were identified with the Guan and Waliser tARget algorithm using seasonally varying IVT percentile thresholds (85th–95th) with a minimum 100 kg m−1 s−1 and geometric filters (length >2,000 km; length-to-width ratio >2). MCS occurrence came from a NOAA CIWRO climatology with size and reflectivity criteria, and MCSs near TCs (within 500 km and 6 hr) were discarded. TC locations were taken from HURDAT2.
supporting_quote: The ARs were detected using an algorithm developed by Guan and Waliser (2015, 2019).
IVT threshold ... 85th to 95th percentile ... with a lower limit of 100 kg m−1 s − 1
Further filtering ... length of IVT >2,000 km and length‐to‐width ratio >2.
MCSs tracked within 500 km and 6 hr of TCs are discarded.
HURDAT2 ... was used to identify the locations of TCs in the SEUS.

chunks.text: Extreme QPF verification compared GEFS reforecast QPF against PRISM QPE using both error statistics and categorical skill metrics. Error metrics included mean error (ME), mean absolute error (MAE), and root mean square error over the study box. Event-based verification used a 95th percentile QPE threshold of 15 mm to compute frequency bias (BIA), probability of detection (POD), false alarm ratio (FAR), and critical success index (CSI). These were evaluated by synoptic pattern and lead time.
supporting_quote: Precipitation error is defined as the difference between QPF and QPE. Pattern‐wise error statistics such as mean error (ME), mean absolute error (MAE), and root mean square error were calculated
We selected the 95th percentile QPE value of 15 mm as the threshold for calculating skill metrics
The critical success index (CSI) ... is the fraction of hits to all possible events (hits, misses, and false alarms).

chunks.text: Observed precipitation was taken from the PRISM daily Quantitative Precipitation Estimate (QPE) product on a 4 km grid with 0.1 mm precision. Wet days were defined when domain-averaged precipitation exceeded 0.01 mm, and extremes were selected by a 90th percentile DAP threshold of 10 mm across wet days. PRISM is based on gauge stations interpolated using terrain and includes radar-aided methods that help represent summer convective precipitation variability in the SEUS. The analysis period is 2001–2019.

interpolated to a 4 km × 4 km grid
Wet days are defined as days when the domain‐averaged precipitation (DAP) ... exceeds 0.01 mm (n = 795).
EPEs are identified ... using a 90th percentile DAP threshold of 10 mm across wet days.

chunks.text: Synoptic and thermodynamic variables used for clustering and composites were obtained from ERA5 reanalysis at 0.25° resolution with hourly output and 37 pressure levels. Variables were sampled at 0000 UTC at three reference stations (KJAN, KBNA, KATL) for clustering inputs, and broader CONUS fields were used for pattern characterization. Values below the surface due to pressure-level interpolation were masked using GMTED2010 elevation data at 1 km resolution. This ensured consistency in regions of complex terrain.
supporting_quote: ERA5 ... available at 0.25° × 0.25° horizontal resolution, 37 pressure levels, and hourly temporal resolution
Surface pressure, surface‐based CAPE, specific humidity at 700 and 850 hPa, and horizontal winds and temperature at the 850, 700, and 500 hPa levels at KJAN, KBNA, and KATL, were used as inputs
all variables below the surface were masked using elevation data from GMTED2010 at a 1 km spatial resolution

chunks.text: Forecast precipitation was taken from NOAA’s Phase 2 GEFS reforecast (GEFS-R v12) product, initialized at 0000 UTC with five ensemble members, available for 2001–2019. The control-member 0.25° QPF was aggregated into day-1 (12–36 h), day-2 (36–60 h), and day-3 (60–84 h) accumulations to align with PRISM QPE at 1200 UTC. The QPF was regridded to the QPE grid using bilinear interpolation. These forecasts were used to compute pattern-wise QPF skill.

forecast hours 12–36, 36–60, and 60–84 were aggregated as QPF at day 1, day 2, and day 3 lead times

chunks.text: KMeans clustering identified six synoptic patterns associated with SEUS extreme precipitation days (2001–2019), with clear seasonality: CS1–CS3 (cool season), TS1 (transition), and WS1–WS2 (warm season). The patterns differ in precipitation distribution and spatial extent: CS2 and CS3, TS1, and WS1 tend to produce larger spatial-scale EPEs, while WS2 produces smaller-extent precipitation and lower likelihood of exceeding the 95th percentile. Cool-season patterns often show stronger 700 hPa winds and orographic enhancement in eastern Tennessee.
supporting_quote: The extreme precipitation days were classified into six synoptic patterns
named according to their occurrences during the cool season ... as CS1, CS2, and CS3 ... transition ... as TS1 ... warm season ... as WS1 and WS2.
cool season pattern, CS2, has the higher probability of precipitation above the 95th percentile, whereas ... WS2 ... precipitation below the 95th percentile.

chunks.text: Storm-type frequencies differ substantially by synoptic pattern. AR occurrence is highest in cool-season patterns (notably CS2) and also high in TS1 and WS2, while TCs are concentrated in the WS1 pattern. MCSs are frequent in warm and some cool/transition patterns, and importantly often coincide with ARs rather than occurring independently. The paper reports specific percentages of days with ARs, MCSs, and TCs in each pattern, enabling pattern-based attribution of EPE mechanisms.

WS1 has the highest contribution of TCs

chunks.text: A substantial fraction of EPEs are linked to coincident ARs and MCSs, varying by season/pattern. The study finds that about 35% of events in CS2, 24% in TS1, and 29% in WS2 involve both ARs and MCSs, quantifying a previously noted but not well-measured mixed-process contribution. This supports the idea that some SEUS extremes are hybrid events with both dynamical moisture transport and convective organization. Such mixed events are common in patterns with strong shear (CS2, TS1) or high CAPE (WS2).
supporting_quote: Nearly 35% of the events in CS2, 24% in TS1, and 54% in WS2 were associated with both ARs and MCSs.
This study identified that nearly 35% of EPEs in CS2, 24% in TS1, and 29% in WS2 were associated with coincident ARs and MCSs.
strong deep layer shear of ∼29 and 34 m s − 1 over the SEUS in CS2 and TS1 ... and the highest CAPE of ∼979 J kg−1 in WS2

chunks.text: Domain-averaged environmental properties distinguish patterns and align with storm-type prevalence. CS2 has the highest mean IVT (503 kg m−1 s−1) and relatively strong shear, supporting frequent ARs and enhanced moisture transport. WS2 has the highest CAPE (979 J kg−1) and highest IWV (46 kg m−2), supporting convective extremes but with smaller spatial scale. WS1 shows high IWV (~42 kg m−2) consistent with TC influence.

chunks.text: GEFS-R underforecasts extreme precipitation on average across the synoptic patterns and shows notable spatial errors in mountainous terrain. The composite difference (QPF − QPE) indicates significant underforecasting of orographic precipitation in eastern Tennessee. Pattern-wise mean error distributions also show predominant underforecast bias. These biases affect both cool-season and warm-season patterns but are especially consequential where orographic enhancement contributes to EPE magnitude.
supporting_quote: the GEFS‐R significantly underforecasts orographic precipitation in eastern Tennessee.
The probability distribution of ME (QPF− QPE) ... shows that the GEFS‐R underforecasts extreme precipitation across all patterns.

chunks.text: The annual day-1 GEFS-R extreme QPF skill for SEUS events above the 90th percentile (10 mm) has a mean CSI of 0.65. Interannual variability in CSI is linked to storm-type frequency: higher-skill years (CSI > 0.5) correspond to more ARs, and years with multiple TCs (e.g., 2004, 2005, 2017) also show CSI > 0.5. This indicates that large-scale, moisture-transport-driven events are comparatively predictable in this framework.
supporting_quote: The annual day‐1 GEFS‐R QPF skill ... when DAP exceeded the 90th percentile (10 mm), is 0.65
years with higher QPF skill (CSI >0.5) were associated with a higher number of ARs while years with lower QPF skill (CSI <0.5) had less number of ARs
The SEUS experienced more than five TCs during 2004, 2005, and 2017 which also had higher QPF skill (CSI >0.5).

chunks.text: Extreme QPF skill depends on synoptic pattern and storm type. Cool-season patterns generally have higher skill than warm-season patterns, and patterns with higher frequency of ARs or TCs show better performance than those dominated by independent MCS activity. The cool-season pattern CS2, characterized by high IVT and frequent ARs, maintains CSI > 0.5 and lower FAR across multiple lead times. Conversely, warm-season WS2 (high CAPE, frequent MCSs) has relatively lower CSI (<0.5) at 1–3 day lead times and exhibits strong underforecast frequency bias.
supporting_quote: The cool season patterns exhibit overall higher QPF skill than the warm season patterns.
patterns with a higher frequency of ARs ... and TCs (WS1) demonstrate higher QPF skill than those dominated by independent MCSs (WS2).
cool‐season pattern CS2 ... contains CSI >0.5 and a lower FAR across multiple lead times.
warm‐ season pattern, WS2, with high CAPE ... contained relatively lower QPF skill (CSI <0.5) at lead times of 1, 2, and 3 days.

chunks.text: Error magnitude varies by pattern, with higher MAE in patterns featuring frequent coincident ARs and MCSs. Specifically, MAE is higher in CS2 and TS1, where extremes are triggered by combined dynamical (moisture transport, shear) and thermodynamical influences. This suggests hybrid events may be harder to quantify accurately even when categorical skill can be relatively high for AR-related patterns. The finding helps separate predictability from amplitude error across regimes.
supporting_quote: The MAE ... is higher in CS2 and TS1, which had a higher frequency of coincident ARs and MCSs
where EPEs were triggered by both dynamical and thermodynamical influences occurring together.

chunks.text: The authors note that their QPF evaluation is constrained to a specific forecast product and limited lead times. Skill assessment uses the GEFS-R control member at 0.25° resolution and examines only 1–3 day lead times. Because resolution and model choice can affect precipitation representation (especially convective and orographic extremes), the reported skill relationships may change with higher-resolution or different forecast systems. The study suggests extending evaluations accordingly.
supporting_quote: The QPF skill evaluation in this study is limited to the GEFS‐R product at a 0.25‐degree resolution and 3‐day lead times.
Future evaluations could consider additional precipitation forecasts at finer resolutions and longer lead times

chunks.text: The paper proposes that the methodology could be scaled beyond the selected SEUS subdomain to larger regions and different hydrologic units. The present analysis focuses on a specific box within the SEUS and uses station-sampled variables for clustering, which may limit generalization without re-tuning for other domains. Extending to CONUS or basin scales could reveal additional patterns and storm-type contributions not captured here. The authors frame this as a pathway for broader applicability rather than a validated result.
supporting_quote: The methodology applied in this study could be extended to classify synoptic patterns that cause extreme precipitation across the entire CONUS
assess extreme QPF skill at various spatial scales, including for individual basins or watersheds.

chunks.text: For patterns with lower QPF skill, the authors recommend targeted modeling case studies to diagnose uncertainty sources. This implies that the current pattern-based diagnostics do not fully explain the physical error mechanisms, especially for thermodynamically driven warm-season regimes. Such follow-on work could improve representation of key processes and potentially enhance predictability at longer lead times. The discussion positions this as needed future work rather than accomplished analysis.
supporting_quote: modeling case studies within patterns with lower QPF skill could provide insights into the sources of uncertainty
allowing for better representation of these processes and enhanced predictability at longer lead times.

chunks.text: Six seasonally distinct synoptic patterns were identified for SEUS EPEs (2001–2019): three cool-season (CS1–CS3), one transition (TS1), and two warm-season (WS1–WS2). Patterns associated with synoptic-scale storm types (ARs, TCs) tend to produce larger-extent precipitation. Mixed-process extremes are common, with sizable shares of events involving coincident ARs and MCSs. These results provide a storm-type and pattern framework for interpreting SEUS extremes.
supporting_quote: Six patterns were identified ... three coolseason patterns (CS1, CS2, and CS3), two warm season patterns (WS1 and WS2), and one transition season pattern (TS1).
This study identified that nearly 35% of EPEs in CS2, 24% in TS1, and 29% in WS2 were associated with coincident ARs and MCSs.
cool season patterns (CS2 and CS3) ... and the warm season pattern (WS1) result in EPEs with a large spatial extent

chunks.text: Predictability varies strongly by pattern and storm type: AR- and TC-related regimes are more predictable than MCS-dominated convective regimes in the SEUS. The cool-season CS2 pattern, with high IVT and frequent ARs, achieves CSI > 0.5 across multiple lead times. The warm-season WS2 pattern, characterized by high CAPE and frequent MCSs, has lower CSI (<0.5) at 1–3 day lead times, reflecting challenges in forecasting thermodynamically driven convective extremes. Thus, high-IVT ARs and AR–MCS mixtures can be forecasted with longer lead time than independent MCS events.
supporting_quote: cool‐season pattern, CS2, with high IVT and higher frequency of ARs contained relatively higher QPF skill (CSI >0.5)
warm‐ season pattern, WS2, with high CAPE and a higher frequency of MCSs contained relatively lower QPF skill (CSI <0.5) at lead times of 1, 2, and 3 days.
extreme precipitation caused by ARs or a mixture of high IVT ARs and MCSs could potentially be forecasted with a relatively longer lead time than independent MCSs in the SEUS.

chunks.text: Hydrologic and hydraulic researchers increasingly rely on in situ time series as references for understanding processes, calibrating/validating simulations, and supporting data-driven models. Modern digital and acoustic instruments provide high-temporal-resolution measurements, but they also increase the volume of data needing conditioning. Data preprocessing (cleaning and conditioning) is therefore essential to extract usable information from raw measurements affected by perturbations and measurement uncertainties.
supporting_quote: The main goal for the hydrologic and hydraulic data producer is to provide trustful in situ datasets that accurately replicate the targeted processes
The immediate processes necessary in preparing the acquired experimental evidence for usage are data cleaning (for removing outliers) and data conditioning over time and space

chunks.text: Flood wave propagation in natural channels exhibits hysteresis and complex multivariate dependencies, especially around hydrograph peaks. High-resolution monitoring methods (e.g., index-velocity and continuous slope-area) expose phase shifts and looped relationships between variables, but noise and perturbations can obscure peak magnitude, timing, and gradients. Accurate peak characterization is crucial for developing and generalizing insights into unsteady open-channel flow behavior.
supporting_quote: Of special importance for the present context is to capture the multivariate dependencies of the hydrographs around their peaks.
These peaks are essential in defining analytical dependencies between the variables, with both the exact magnitude and timing of the peak being crucial for analysis.

chunks.text: The growing literature on denoising and smoothing does not provide clear recommendations on which preprocessing methods are optimal for river-flow time series. Many techniques are in use (e.g., WT, EMD, HHT, Savitzky-Golay), and a substantial fraction of approaches fall into an 'Others' category, indicating ongoing development and lack of consensus. This motivates systematic testing and screening of candidate smoothing methods under practical hydrometric conditions.
supporting_quote: The above studies do not offer clear-cut recommendations on the efficiency of various types of preprocessing and smoothing methods.
The fact that the "Others" category represents 33% of the used methods ... indicates that the smoothing algorithms are still in development.

chunks.text: The study aims to identify optimal techniques for smoothing hydrologic and hydraulic data acquired at high sampling rates during unsteady flows in natural rivers. It evaluates multiple smoothing methods on measured variables (index velocity, stage, and free-surface slope) with emphasis on accurately preserving peak magnitude and peak timing. The work intends to produce practical guidance for future data acquisition/processing and to better support data-driven modeling.
supporting_quote: The primary objective of this study is to ascertain optimal techniques for smoothing hydrologic and hydraulic data acquired with high sampling rates in unsteady flows
The goal of this analysis is to set a mathematical foundation for empirical results ... formulating practical guidance for future data acquisition and processing

chunks.text: A specific goal is to develop a sequential screening protocol that combines quantitative statistical fitness parameters with qualitative expert judgments. This protocol is meant to narrow the choice among many available smoothing methods and to evaluate robustness to data frequency and signal-to-noise differences. The peak-focused performance metrics are intended to preserve meaningful hydrodynamic features while filtering unwanted noise and perturbations.
supporting_quote: This study presents a new screening protocol to smoothen streamflow data from unwanted influences and noise
The protocol combines quantitative (statistical fitness parameters) and qualitative (domain expert judgments) evaluations.

chunks.text: In situ hydrometric time series can contain points that do not represent the targeted process due to measurement noise, small signal magnitudes, and insufficient sampling resolution. These issues are common in stream discharge estimation where variables change widely during storm inputs. Without robust conditioning, noise can dominate and obscure the true dynamics.
supporting_quote: the acquired data points might not even illustrate the targeted processes. One example is when the magnitude of measured variables is small, with the data points embedded within the measurement noise.
Another example is when sampling the flow with temporal resolutions that are not sufficient to capture the frequencies of the flow variability.

chunks.text: Signals from modern stream monitoring methods (especially index velocity and free-surface slope) are persistently noisy due to environmental factors and sensor-induced errors. This noise is particularly problematic around hydrograph peaks, where precise magnitude and timing are required to analyze hysteresis and phasing among variables. Slope derived from stages at two locations can be especially error-sensitive.
supporting_quote: the useful signals are contaminated by environmental factors present at the site ... as well from sensorinduced errors
Smith et al. (2010) note that an error of about 0.03 m in the fall of the free surface can lead to a discharge estimated with the CSA method that is off by about 25%.

chunks.text: Hydrographs may contain real flow perturbations ('pulses') superposed on the main wave, complicating the distinction between meaningful variability and noise. Pulses can introduce local peaks or inflection points in different variables, especially near the flood crest. Smoothing must avoid removing these physically meaningful features while still reducing noise.
supporting_quote: We define pulses as groups of consecutive data points on flow-variable hydrographs reflecting a flow acceleration–deceleration cycle.
The presence of the pulses complicates the interpretation of the overall flood wave, characterization especially when they occur close to the flood crest

chunks.text: Selecting a smoothing method is overwhelming because different methods yield different results and true values are unavailable for direct ground-truthing. Literature comparisons rarely yield clear-cut recommendations and performance depends on method parameters and data context. This creates a need for a structured selection workflow rather than ad hoc choices.
supporting_quote: the choice of method used for cleaning the data is overwhelming due to a lack of clarity on the optimum method to be used.
each method provides a slightly different result and the true values of the measurements are not available for ground-truthing.

chunks.text: The study tests a set of 18 smoothing algorithms spanning simple moving averages and advanced decomposition/transform approaches. The methods include multiple moving-average variants, exponential smoothing, regression-based smoothing, kernel/LOWESS, EMD, DWT, FSS, Savitzky–Golay, HHT, and Whittaker–Henderson smoothing. Methods and parameters are compared to find candidates that best preserve hydrograph peaks while reducing unwanted noise.
supporting_quote: It is tested with 18 smoothing methods to identify optimal data conditioning candidates.
Table 1. The smoothing algorithms tested in this study.

chunks.text: A four-step sequential screening protocol evaluates smoothing performance, emphasizing peak magnitude and peak timing. Steps 1–3 are quantitative filters using percent differences, MAPE, and peak time shifts, and Step 4 combines RMSE with expert visual inspection of hydrograph shape. Thresholds include excluding methods with average differences of 10% or greater and eliminating time shifts larger than 20 data points (5 h in 15-min records).
supporting_quote: Methods exhibiting average differences of 10% or greater are excluded
The protocols that displayed time shifts larger than 20 data points (equivalent to 5 h in the 15-min records) are eliminated.
Step 4 of the smoothing procedure screening is predicated by the evaluation of the root mean square error (RMSE) value ... in conjunction with visual inspection

chunks.text: Step 1 computes average error percentages between raw sampled values and the smoothed trend line at the sampling times, removing methods exceeding the specified tolerance. Step 2 computes MAPE on retained methods and removes those with MAPE values exceeding 10. This staged filtering is intended to reduce the candidate pool before examining peak timing behavior.
supporting_quote: In the first step ... quantified by the magnitude of the average error percentages ... Methods exhibiting average differences of 10% or greater are excluded
During the second screening step, the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) is computed ... Datasets with MAPE values exceeding 10 are removed.

chunks.text: Step 3 explicitly screens for peak timing distortions by comparing peak shifts between smoothed and observed time series. Methods producing time shifts beyond 20 data points are eliminated, reflecting the need to preserve peak timing for flood-crest analysis. This step recognizes that low error magnitudes alone are insufficient if timing is biased.
supporting_quote: In the third step of the screening, the evaluation of the smoothing methods is made based on the magnitude of the peak shifts
The protocols that displayed time shifts larger than 20 data points ... are eliminated.

chunks.text: Visual inspection is used as an expert-judgment layer to assess whether smoothed traces preserve expected hysteresis-related trends and multi-peak behavior near crests. The paper notes that multi-peak features near the peak may be real fluctuations rather than noise, and smoothing window choices can shift magnitude and time. Therefore, qualitative criteria are used to judge allowable shifts around the perceived overall peak.
supporting_quote: The role of the visual inspections is to compare the smoothened data trace with the expected trends predicted by expert knowledge on the hysteretic behavior.
The multi-peak feature is not expected to be induced by noise. Rather, it might be attributed to the fluctuations of the flows that are inherent in natural-scale open channel flows.

chunks.text: The evaluation produced 118 smoothed datasets by varying method parameters (e.g., spans, weights, functions, wavelet types). Implementations were carried out in both R and MATLAB using specific packages for different smoothers. Computational limitations affected applicability of some methods, with WHS noted as impractical for the full-year 15-min dataset without high-performance computing.
supporting_quote: A total of 118 datasets were generated by employing various smoothing techniques, with each technique being applied using distinct smoothing parameters and spans.
The numerical and graphical evaluations were executed with the programming language R and the MATLAB analysis platform.
The WHS method was only applied to the 1 h data ... requires high-performance computing, which was not available

chunks.text: The main testbed dataset is a 2015 time series of raw index-velocity measured every 15 minutes at USGS gaging station #05558300 on the Henry River in Illinois. The year 2015 was chosen because it contains the largest storm among six years analyzed at this station. Ten major storms in 2015 were selected for detailed smoothing evaluation around peaks.
supporting_quote: raw (as sampled) index-velocity data acquired every 15 min at a United States Geological Survey (USGS) gaging station on Henry River in Illinois (USGS #05558300) for the year 2015.
The year 2015 was selected ... as it contains the largest storm in the 6 years of records.
The 2015 data sample selected for testing includes 10 major storms

chunks.text: To examine sampling-frequency impacts, an hourly (1 h) index-velocity dataset was derived from the 15-min series by uniformly discarding three consecutive points starting with the initial point. The same screening protocol was applied to the 1 h data for the same set of 10 major storms. This allows direct comparison of smoothing performance under reduced temporal resolution.
supporting_quote: The screening procedure was also applied to the 1 h data time series for the index-velocity data acquired for the 10 major storms
This data was obtained from the 15-min indexvelocity dataset ... by uniformly discarding three consecutive points starting with the initial point

chunks.text: Additional site testing used 10-min index-velocity data from the Yeongsang River (South Korea) at gaging station #5004550 near Naju Bridge. The site is about 150 m wide at base flow with bed slope 0.00025, and the finer sampling was expected to benefit smoothing. Evaluation focused on the largest storm in 2020 to test generality and scalability across conditions.
supporting_quote: Yeongsang River (South Korea) at gaging station #5004550 located near Naju Bridge.
the river is about 150 m wide (at based flow) and has a bed slope of 0.00025. The sampling rate for the index-velocity data is 10 min
The numerical evaluations were made on the largest storm in 2020.

chunks.text: Free-surface slope smoothing was evaluated using slope estimated from stage measured at two points along a stream. Two contrasting sites were used: Naju Bridge (10-min sampling) and Clear Creek near Oxford, Iowa (15-min sampling) with a small channel (~10 m wide) and bed slope 0.0004. The Clear Creek example used the largest storm of 2022.
supporting_quote: the measured stage of the free surface acquired at two observation points along the stream.
Clear Creek in Iowa ... about 10 m wide at baseflow) with a bed slope of 0.0004.
The data for the slope estimation is collected at a sampling rate of 10 min at the first site and 15 min at the second one for the largest storm of the year 2022.

chunks.text: Applying the screening protocol to the full-year 15-min index-velocity series eliminated multiple methods stepwise and retained seven top performers: DWT, 3p/5p/7p/9p moving average, kernel smoothing, and exponential smoothing. Table-based metrics across 10 storms show DWT with RMSE 0.005, MAPE 0.923, and 10/10 visual passes, outperforming others overall. Exponential smoothing met many visual checks but had comparatively worse errors and peak shifts.
supporting_quote: led to the elimination of ... LOWESS, GS, QR, and LR (in step 1), EMD (in step 2), FSS and SG (in step 3), and HHT, 3p Weighted Moving Average (WMA), and 3p Exponential Moving Average (EMA) (in step 4).
Table 2... DWT | RMSE 0.005 | MAPE 0.923 ... Visual check passes (10 storms) 10

it can be observed that while the Exponential smoothing (ES) technique meets the criteria for most visual assessments, it exhibits inferior performance in terms of error magnitudes and temporal shifts

chunks.text: Among the seven retained 15-min methods, DWT ranked best in the combined criteria of error magnitudes, temporal shifts, and visual inspections. In Table 2, DWT has the lowest peak magnitude difference comparable to the best methods and fewer peak shifts than many alternatives. The paper emphasizes DWT’s strength particularly when evaluated over the larger year-long dataset.
supporting_quote: DWT emerges as the most effective method based on its better performance in terms of error magnitudes, temporal shifts, and visual inspections
Table 2... DWT ... % Difference in peak magnitude 0.544 ... Time shifts in the peaks 5

chunks.text: Visual evaluation around peaks indicates that small-window moving averages (3–5 point) preserve multiple local peaks near the crest, while larger windows (7–9 point) damp these features. Several non-MA methods (including DWT and KS in some cases) may smooth away local peaks around the overall storm peak. Exponential smoothing visibly shifts magnitude and timing relative to other best methods for the illustrated storms.
supporting_quote: using the 3–5p MA methods produces several peaks around the wave crest. This feature is gradually weakened for the 7–9p MA methods
An exception is the ES method, which is visibly shifted in magnitude and timing for all three individual storms

chunks.text: Smoothing outcomes can depend on whether methods are applied to the full-year series or to individual storm windows. For moving averages (3–9 point), results were consistent across year-long vs event-long processing. In contrast, KS, ES, and DWT produced noticeably different patterns when applied to shorter storm time spans, and WHS performed effectively when applied to an individual storm span.
supporting_quote: The plots ... demonstrate that the 3-5-7-9p MA methods yielded consistent agreement regardless of whether the entire year's data or the storms' data are used.
It is also apparent that KS, ES and DWT reveal quite different dataset patterns.
Notable is the high level of effectiveness for the WHS applied to the time span of an individual storm

chunks.text: For the derived 1 h index-velocity dataset, the optimal set shifted relative to the 15-min case. Table 3 lists six best methods, with 7pMA achieving the highest number of visual passes (8/10). Based on the visual evaluations for storms 1, 4, and 10, the study concludes that 7pMA was the most appropriate smoother for the 1 h data.
supporting_quote: Table 3... 7pMA ... Visual check passes (10 storms) 8
Based on the evaluation results shown in [Figs. 11–13] it appears that the most appropriate smoothing technique for 1-h data is the 7pMA.

chunks.text: At the South Korea Naju Bridge site using 10-min index-velocity data, visual inspection suggested 3p MA, KS, and WHS closely followed raw-data trends, while DWT was also acceptable. WHS was judged best among the tested methods. Several methods (GS, LR, QR, FSS) failed to track the signal, and ES and SG showed significant magnitude and time shifts.
supporting_quote: The visual inspection ... suggests that the 3p MA approach, KS and WHS follow closely the trends indicated by the raw data.
Out of the set of optimal methods, WHS performs the best.
The worst-performing methods are the GS, LR, QR, and FSS approaches ... and the ES and SG approaches, which show significant magnitude and time shifts

chunks.text: For free-surface slope at Naju Bridge, multiple methods (GS, LR, FSS, QR) produced linear trends below observed values, replicating issues seen in index-velocity smoothing at that site. DWT, KS, and MA-based approaches were considered successful, but WHS was identified as the optimal method for slope smoothing there. This highlights variable- and site-dependence of smoothing performance.
supporting_quote: An inspection of the results ... reveals that GS, LR, FFS, and QR exhibit consistent linear trends much below the observed data values

While the approaches of DWT, KS, and MA have demonstrated successful results, it can be argued that the optimal smoothing algorithm for the free-surface slope was acquired at this site using the WHS technique.

chunks.text: For free-surface slope at Clear Creek (Iowa), the best-performing methods differed from Naju Bridge. Only the 5-point moving average closely approximated raw trends among MA methods, with KS and DWT also efficient. Exponential smoothing showed a large time shift, and FSS/SG/WHS clustered but with a large magnitude shift; FSS also produced several peaks.
supporting_quote: Out of all the tested MA-based methods, it seems that only the 5-p MA method closely approximates the trends indicated by the raw data
The ES method displays a large time shift compared to all other methods

The FSS, SG, and WHS methods are close together ... but the shift in magnitude is quite large. FSS may first appear to provide effective smoothing, but it ultimately leads to the presence of several peaks

chunks.text: The paper argues smoothing is preferable to filtering in this application because noise and unwanted fluctuations are hard to distinguish from real variability that must be preserved. Visual inspection provides a controlled evaluation environment to ensure important patterns remain, but this depends on assumptions and tuning choices. The work explicitly notes smoothing challenges linked to parameter selection and the reasonableness of method assumptions.
supporting_quote: In our case the unwanted fluctuations and noise are not easily distinguished from the actual variabilities that must be preserved.
There are also multiple challenges when implementing smoothing as these techniques rely on the reasonableness of the assumptions and the selection of the tuning parameters

chunks.text: Expert-driven visual criteria are subjective, and judgments depend on user skills and familiarity with hysteresis processes. The presence of multiple local peaks near the overall crest complicates deciding what is noise versus physical pulses. The paper treats this subjectivity as a necessary complement to quantitative metrics rather than a fully automatable step.
supporting_quote: The visual criteria are subjective as they depend on the users' skills and familiarity with the hysteresis process associated with unsteady open-channel flow.
The judgment of the visual appearance is complicated by the presence of multiple local smaller peaks in the vicinity of the overall flood wave peaks

chunks.text: Sensitivity analyses show smoothing outcomes vary with hydrograph shape and the time span selected for analysis (year-long vs storm-only), reflecting nonlinearity and iterative characteristics of methods. The paper suggests parameter adjustments can remediate mismatches, but also proposes future subsetting of storms by generic parameters to improve applicability. This emphasizes that a single universal method is unlikely across event types.
supporting_quote: the same method when applied to different peak hydrograph shapes performed slightly differently. Similarly, the length of the time span for the data subject to smoothing can produce slightly different results.
A possible remediation ... is the subsetting of the storm types based on a generic set of parameters

chunks.text: Method performance is constrained by computational resources and dataset size. WHS was not feasible for the whole year of 15-min data because it produced large-size data requiring high-performance computing, so it was applied only to smaller datasets or reduced-frequency data. This limits direct comparisons of WHS under all conditions evaluated for other methods.
supporting_quote: WHS could be only applied for smaller size datasets.
for processing the whole year of 15-min data this procedure produces large-size data that requires high-performance computing, which was not available for the present study.

chunks.text: The authors caution that assessment is not exhaustive because only a limited number of smoothing procedures and datasets were analyzed. Although the datasets were chosen to be statistically and physically significant, results are framed as preliminary and intended to highlight considerations rather than provide a single definitive recipe. This caveat reinforces the need for context-specific screening.
supporting_quote: We are aware that the performance assessment is not exhaustive as we analyzed a limited number of smoothing procedures and datasets.
providing the researcher with an exact recipe may not be feasible due to the unique characteristics of each hydrological or meteorological event

chunks.text: The study concludes that a structured screening protocol combining statistical metrics and expert visual evaluation can guide selection of smoothing methods for noisy unsteady-flow datasets, with a focus on hydrograph peaks. Across the tests, MA-based methods (3p, 5p, 7p, 9p) were categorized as highly efficient. The protocol is positioned as practical guidance for improving data reliability used in hydrologic/hydraulic analyses and modeling.
supporting_quote: The study introduces a screening protocol aimed at conditioning flow variables acquired under different conditions using adaptive and rigorous statistical measures
Highly efficient: 3p, 5-p, 7-p, and 9-p MA-based methods.

chunks.text: The paper finds that simpler smoothing tools can outperform more intricate methods for preserving peak magnitude and timing, depending on dataset characteristics. It reports that moving-average approaches often yield highly effective outcomes, while some more computationally demanding methods can be inferior. This supports the recommendation to systematically test and tune methods rather than assuming complexity implies superiority.
supporting_quote: employing basic techniques such as moving average approaches ... can yield highly effective smoothing outcomes, whereas more intricate methods with more computational demands may produce inferior results.
The above inferences demonstrate that, in certain cases, employing basic techniques ... can yield highly effective smoothing outcomes

chunks.text: The authors emphasize that the proposed workflow improves confidence in extracting meaningful information from complex, noisy monitoring data, supporting better understanding and prediction of unsteady-flow processes. They highlight future directions such as integrating smoothing with machine learning for more adaptive conditioning. The work frames its contribution as a systematic approach that enhances reliability of hydrologic and meteorological data analyses.
supporting_quote: With increasing experience with the screening workflow ... enabling the implementation of the process through machine learning techniques rather than user intervention.
exploring the integration of smoothing techniques with machine learning approaches could lead to more adaptive and data-driven data conditioning methods.

chunks.text: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are an emerging photovoltaic technology because they combine high power conversion efficiency with comparatively low production costs. The paper notes that single-junction PSCs have already reached efficiencies above 26%, approaching the performance of mature silicon photovoltaics. Understanding perovskite crystal structure and device-layer functions is presented as foundational for further improvements in performance and stability.
supporting_quote: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have become an attractive alternative energy option due to their high photovoltaic conversion efficiency (PCE) and low production costs
single-junction PSCs have thus far achieved a PCE exceeding 26.1%

chunks.text: PSCs commonly use either regular (n-i-p) or inverted (p-i-n) planar architectures. In regular devices the stack is TCO/ETL/perovskite/HTL/metal, while inverted devices swap the ETL and HTL positions. Charge generation in the perovskite is followed by selective extraction of holes by the HTL and electrons by the ETL and their collection at electrodes.
supporting_quote: two typical structures of PSCs can be constructed: inverted-type (inverted planar) and regular-type (direct planar)
Direct planar PSCs have functional layers arranged from bottom to top: a transparent conductive oxide (TCO...)), ETL, perovskite layer, HTL, and metal electrode

chunks.text: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are organic molecular assemblies that spontaneously adsorb onto surfaces. The review frames SAMs as comprising an anchoring headgroup, a linker/spacer, and a terminal functional group. Because SAMs can form ordered ultrathin films on transparent conductive oxides, they are positioned as promising selective-contact layers in PSCs.
supporting_quote: SAMs of organic molecules are molecular assemblies formed spontaneously on surfaces by adsorption
SAMs consist of three components: the headgroup or anchoring group, the spacer or linker, and the terminal or functional group

chunks.text: The review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of SAM utilization in PSCs, emphasizing SAMs as hole-transport/selective-contact layers. It also includes SAM structure, preparation, adsorption/binding understanding, and device-application examples. A secondary goal is to briefly cover SAMs used as electron-transport layers and discuss prospects for commercial integration.
supporting_quote: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the utilization of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), with a specific focus on their potential as hole transport layers (HTLs).
We also discuss their application as electron transport layers.

chunks.text: The review specifically focuses on integrating SAMs into inverted PSCs as novel selective-contact HTLs. It is written to guide researchers seeking improved efficiency and stability by rational SAM design, interface engineering, and consideration of scalability. The paper also aims to outline challenges and future research directions for SAM technology in PSCs.
supporting_quote: This review focuses on integrating SAMs on inverted PSCs, particularly in novel selective-contact HTLs, to guide researchers wishing to enhance the efficiency and stability of PSCs.
The challenges of using SAMs as a functional layer are discussed, with suggestions for future design and development of SAMs.

chunks.text: Conventional functional layers used in PSCs present performance and stability limitations that motivate alternative selective contacts. The paper summarizes drawbacks such as TiO2 band mismatch, hysteresis and UV instability; C60 solubility and cost issues; and HTLs like Spiro-OMeTAD and PEDOT:PSS suffering from volatility, moisture sensitivity, and interface problems. These issues can increase cost and hinder commercialization.
supporting_quote: Table 3 Summary of potential limits of the functional layers used in PSCs.
PEDOT:PSS... the natural acidity of PEDOT:PSS solutions can lead to the severe corrosion of ITO electrodes and perovskite.

chunks.text: SAM-based HTLs are difficult to characterize at the microstructural level because they are ultrathin organic monolayers on complex metal-oxide surfaces. Standard measurements can confirm formation but often cannot reveal monolayer defects, continuity, or the detailed state of adsorption. This contributes to ongoing debate about whether SAMs mainly tune work function or also assist charge extraction/transport.
supporting_quote: Characterizing the microstructure of SAM-based HTLs... is complex due to their fine structure.
these methods fail to reveal the monolayers' detailed state on such complex surfaces, particularly issues like defects and continuity.

chunks.text: The functional role and mechanism of SAMs in PSCs remain controversial, partly because charge transport within a monolayer-thick HTL is hard to probe. The paper notes that the thinness complicates understanding charge transport and leaves open whether performance gains come from work-function modification, improved selectivity, or other interfacial effects. The review argues that more advanced surface/interface-sensitive characterization is needed.
supporting_quote: due to monolayer thinness, understanding the charge transport within these HTLs remains challenging, engendering ongoing debates about their function in modifying work functions or assisting with charge extraction and transport
more advanced surface- and interface-sensitive techniques are necessary to explore the properties and mechanisms of SAM-based HTLs thoroughly.

chunks.text: SAM stability is a concern because SAM-based HTLs are structurally simple and placed on the light-incident side in inverted PSCs. The review highlights risks under thermal and light stress and motivates exploration of stronger anchoring groups and improved molecular backbones to resist degradation. It also notes that commonly used SAMs like MeO-2PACz can degrade under light and electrochemical conditions.
supporting_quote: concerns regarding their thermal and light stability, especially for the SAM-based HTL in single-junction inverted PSCs, wherein the SAM layer is located at the light incident side.
MeO-2PACz... undergoes significant degradation under light and electrochemical conditions.

chunks.text: The paper describes using tolerance factor and octahedral factor as standard quantitative tools to assess perovskite structural stability. Tolerance factor t is computed from ionic radii of A-, B-, and X-site ions, and typical stability ranges are discussed. The octahedral factor μ is defined as rB/rX and used to assess stability of BX6 octahedra.
supporting_quote: t = (rA + rX)/(sqrt(2)(rB + rX))
Another approach... the octahedral factor (μ), which can be expressed as: μ = rB/rX

chunks.text: SAM molecular design is framed around three modular components: anchoring group, linker, and terminal group. Anchoring groups based on chemical bonding are emphasized for solution-processed electronic devices, including phosphonic acid, carboxylic acid, and silane. Linker choice (alkyl vs conjugated) is described as controlling packing, tilt angle, tunneling length, and charge-transfer properties.
supporting_quote: SAMs consist of three components: the headgroup or anchoring group, the spacer or linker, and the terminal or functional group
Commonly used headgroups include... carboxylic acid anchoring group, phosphonic acid anchoring group... or silane anchoring group.

chunks.text: For phosphonic-acid SAMs on metal oxides, the adsorption mechanism is described as –OH protonation/condensation leading to strong P–O–M bonds with possible mono-, bi-, and tridentate binding. Reaction conditions and oxide surface chemistry determine the binding configuration. Tridentate bonding is linked to hydrogen transfer and hetero-condensation with oxygen-vacancy formation.
supporting_quote: it allows for single, bidentate, and tridentate binding modes
condenses to form a strong P–O–M bond

chunks.text: PM-IRRAS/IRRAS are presented as key surface-sensitive spectroscopies to determine SAM vibrational signatures and infer binding modes on ITO and ZnO. Example peaks include v(P=O) at 1230 cm−1 and P–O–(H) stretching at 955 and 930 cm−1, used to distinguish bound vs free groups. The approach is used to argue for predominantly bidentate binding for ODPA on ITO and tridentate binding for ODPA on ZnO.
supporting_quote: v (P=O) vibration at 1230 cm−1 and P-O-(H) stretching vibrations at 955 cm−1 and 930 cm−1
confirming the tridentate attachment

chunks.text: XPS combined with DFT calculations is described as a robust method to identify adsorption geometries of phosphonic acids on metal-oxide substrates. Shifts in O 1s binding energies between ODPA powder and ODPA-modified ITO indicate chemical interaction, and DFT helps assign peak components to specific binding states. The combined analysis identifies bidentate and tridentate binding as predominant on ITO.
supporting_quote: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) coupled with density functional theory (DFT) calculations has been established as a robust method
identified bidentate and tridentate binding as the predominant attachment geometries of phosphonic acids on the ITO surface

chunks.text: To determine SAM molecular orientation, the paper describes using UPS and MAES together with DFT density-of-states calculations. UPS probes valence DOS and MAES probes outermost orbitals, enabling inference of surface orientation from differences between spectra. For 3PATAT-C3, MAES showing strong π-state contribution is used to support a vertical alignment on ITO.
supporting_quote: ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and metastable atom electron spectroscopy (MAES) were employed
The MAES results highlighted a pronounced contribution from π states compared to σ states, indicating that 3PATAT-C3 molecules are vertically aligned on the ITO surface.

chunks.text: The paper compiles ionic radii used for perovskite tolerance-factor calculations, listing common A-site cations (e.g., MA+, FA+, Cs+) and B-site cations (e.g., Pb2+, Sn2+), as well as halides. These values provide inputs for assessing perovskite formability and stability across compositions. Such tabulated radii support the discussion of structural design rules for ABX3 perovskites.
supporting_quote: Table 1 Estimation of A-cation, B-cation, and X-cation radii in ABX3.

chunks.text: Different perovskite compositions are summarized with their tolerance factor t and octahedral factor μ to compare structural stability trends across A-site and halide substitutions. The table includes values such as MAPbI3 (t = 0.912, μ = 0.541) and FAPbI3 (t = 0.987, μ = 0.541). This dataset is used to illustrate how composition shifts move materials toward ideal, distorted, or non-perovskite structures.
supporting_quote: Table 2 The t and μ factors of MABX3, FABX3, and CsBX3.

chunks.text: The review provides a comparative list of limitations for common ETL and HTL materials in PSCs. Examples include TiO2 (band mismatch, hysteresis, poor UV stability), C60 (poor solubility, high purification cost), and PEDOT:PSS (acidity, moisture sensitivity). This tabulated information motivates the move toward SAM-based selective contacts.
supporting_quote: Table 3 Summary of potential limits of the functional layers used in PSCs.
TiO2... Poor UV stability
C60... Poor solubility in common organic solvents.

chunks.text: High-efficiency inverted PSCs using SAMs as HTLs are summarized with photovoltaic metrics. Reported examples include MeO-2PACz with PCE 25.6% and DMAcPA with PCE 25.9%, both showing high FF values near ~85%. This compilation highlights the state-of-the-art performance range achievable with SAM-HTLs.
supporting_quote: Table 4 The latest high-performance inverted PSCs achieving PCEs of over 23% based on a SAM as the HTL.
MeO-2PACz ... PCE (%) 25.6
DMAcPA ... PCE (%) 25.9

chunks.text: The paper lists performance statistics for phosphonic-acid SAM-HTLs in single-junction PSCs, including JSC, VOC, FF, and PCE. Entries include MeO-2PACz (PCE 20.2%), Cos-CbzNaph (PCE 24.02%), and 2PACz+3-MPA (PCE 25.3%). The table serves as a quantitative reference linking specific SAM chemistries to device outcomes.
supporting_quote: Table 5 Performance statistics of SAMs based on phosphonic acid groups as single-junction PSCs for HTLs.
Cos-CbzNaph ... PCE (%) 24.02
2PACz+3-MPA ... PCE ... 25.3

chunks.text: The review compiles performance statistics for carboxylic-acid SAM-HTLs in single-junction PSCs. Reported data include AC-5 with PCE 23.19% and EADR03/EADR04 with PCE around 21%. This dataset allows comparison of carboxylate-anchored SAMs against phosphonate-based systems and conventional polymer HTLs.
supporting_quote: Table 6 Performance statistics of SAMs based on carboxylic acid groups as single-junction PSCs for HTLs.
EADR03 ... PCE 21.2
EADR04 ... PCE 21.0

chunks.text: SAMs are argued to provide cost and processing advantages over conventional HTLs by requiring very low material usage and enabling simpler synthesis/purification. The review claims effective SAM structures are relatively simple and do not require expensive noble-metal catalysts. It also states SAM-based HTLs can be purified by recrystallization rather than column chromatography, aiding scale-up.
supporting_quote: The reported effective SAM structures are relatively simple, with synthesis steps that do not require expensive noble metal catalysts
The molecules of a SAM-based HTL can be purified through recrystallization instead of traditional column chromatography.
Only a small concentration of SAMs is required to fabricate efficient devices

chunks.text: Because SAMs are monolayer-thin, they can reduce parasitic optical losses compared to thicker HTLs such as PEDOT:PSS and NiOx (>10 nm). The paper states that SAM-HTLs maintain optical transparency of ITO/FTO and thus support higher current generation. This is presented as a key reason to adopt SAMs for high-JSC devices and tandem architectures.
supporting_quote: Commonly used hole transport materials like PEDOT:PSS, NiOx, etc. typically have greater thicknesses (> 10 nm)
using SAMs as HTLs does not compromise the optical transparency of the substrate (ITO or FTO)

chunks.text: Phosphonic-acid SAMs can form strong binding configurations on metal oxides, enabling dense and uniform monolayers on ITO/FTO at room temperature. The review highlights multiple binding modes (mono-, bi-, tridentate) that underpin robust adsorption. This strong anchoring is presented as beneficial for stable selective-contact behavior at the TCO/perovskite interface.
supporting_quote: Molecules with phosphonic acid anchoring groups are recognized for their ability to form bidentate solid/tridentate bonds with oxide surfaces.
This results in dense, uniform monolayers forming on various oxides, ITO or FTO, even at room temperature.

chunks.text: Early demonstrations of phosphonic-acid SAM-HTLs showed that mixing a functional SAM with a small co-adsorbent can improve interfacial wetting and device performance. In particular, a mixture of 10% V1036 with 90% n-butylphosphonic acid (C4) produced a PCE of 17.8%. The mixed SAM was also reported to have about 62% of the surface coverage of a pure V1036 SAM.
supporting_quote: Finally, a PCE of 17.8% for a 10% V1036 and 90% C4 mixture SAMs-based HTL device was achieved.
the mixed SAM containing approximately 62% of the surface coverage of a pure V1036 SAM

chunks.text: Spin-coated phosphonic-acid SAMs such as MeO-2PACz and 2PACz were characterized as forming monolayers on ITO, supported by IRRAS evidence of P–O bonding and loss of P–OH features. Devices using 2PACz achieved VOC = 1.19 V and PCE = 20.9% (certified 20.28%). MeO-2PACz-based devices reached PCE around 21.1% and were also applied in tandem contexts.
supporting_quote: IRRAS results indicated that the phosphonic acid-based SAM-HTLs prepared by spin-coating were single-layer rather than multilayer structures
2PACz exhibited a high open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.19 V and a PCE of 20.9 % (certified as 20.28%).

chunks.text: Adjusting carbazole substitution and alkyl chain length in phosphonic-acid SAMs can reduce nonradiative recombination and improve fill factor. The review reports Me-4PACz enabling single-junction FF approaching 84%. In tandem devices, it cites a monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem reaching PCE = 29.15%.
supporting_quote: Consequently, the fill factor (FF) of the single-junction PSCs integrated with Me-4PACz approached 84%.
a single-junction perovskite/silicon tandem solar cell achieved... a remarkable PCE of 29.15%.

chunks.text: Binding-strength comparisons suggest phosphonic acid anchors can adhere more strongly to ITO than sulfonic or carboxylic anchors. DFT adsorption energies on ITO (111) were reported as −2.71 eV for −PO3H2, compared with −2.49 eV for −SO3H and −2.15 eV for −COOH. This stronger binding is linked to improved adhesion, film quality, and charge collection at the interface.
supporting_quote: the -PO3H2 group bonds more robustly to ITO in a tridentate fashion than the -SO3H and -COOH groups
adsorption energy for -PO3H2... -2.71 eV... for -SO3H and -COOH are -2.49 and -2.15 eV, respectively.

chunks.text: Mixed or co-assembled SAM strategies can address incomplete coverage and reduce interfacial recombination, especially on textured substrates. The review describes a co-adsorbent strategy that disassembles phosphonic-acid clusters, yielding improved contact uniformity. This approach achieved a laboratory-measured PCE of 25.3% and a certified quasi-steady-state PCE of 24.8%, with encapsulated devices retaining 95% performance after >1000 h stress testing.
supporting_quote: a co-adsorbent strategy was developed, effectively disassembling high-order clusters
This method achieved a remarkable laboratory-measured PCE of 25.3% and a certified quasi-steady-state PCE of 24.8%.
retaining 95% of its performance after over 1000 h under stress conditions

chunks.text: The review emphasizes that standard characterization tools (XPS, AFM, contact angle) can confirm SAM formation but often cannot resolve defects, continuity, and detailed monolayer state on realistic metal-oxide surfaces. This limits mechanistic understanding and the ability to link microscopic structure to device performance. It calls for more advanced surface- and interface-sensitive techniques to study SAM-based HTLs.
supporting_quote: Techniques like XPS, atomic force microscopy, and water contact-angle measurements are typically used to confirm SAM formation
these methods fail to reveal the monolayers' detailed state on such complex surfaces, particularly issues like defects and continuity.
